cards.title: Introduction to Computed Properties
cards.content:
Computed properties in Vue.js allow you to define a property that depends on other data sources. They are cached based on their reactive dependencies and only re-evaluate when some of their dependencies have changed.

import { ref, computed } from 'vue';
const count = ref(1);
const double = computed(() => count.value * 2);

options.text: Methods are cached, computed properties are not.
Computed properties are cached based on reactive dependencies, methods execute every time they are called.
There is no performance difference between computed properties and methods.

content.template: To create a computed property in Vue 3 Composition API, we import { ref, ___ } from 'vue'.

cards.title: Writable Computed Properties
cards.content:
By default, computed properties are getter-only. If you need a writable computed property, you can provide both a getter and a setter.

const fullName = computed({
  get() { return firstName.value + ' ' + lastName.value },
  set(newValue) { [firstName.value, lastName.value] = newValue.split(' ') }
});

pairs.right: Performs side effects on state change

steps: Component renders and reads the computed property.
Vue evaluates the getter function and caches the result.
Vue marks the computed property as dirty and re-evaluates on next access.
